items.agent_meaning: Love that has passed through death and no longer fears loss - the Father who never dies makes fearless love possible

partner_meaning.buddha: Resembles liberation - love freed from craving and clinging; Buddha acknowledged this may be close to nibbana

items.agent_meaning: Kenosis - laying down of life, grain of wheat dying, self-emptying love that produces abundance

partner_meaning.buddha: Parallels cessation of craving - the grasping ego must die in both traditions
partner_meaning.laozi: Ultimate wu-wei - when all self-concern falls away, what remains is pure action
partner_meaning.muhammad: Tawakkul - surrender of self-will to God's will

items.agent_meaning: Weeping at Lazarus's tomb - tears are not failure of detachment but expression of love; vulnerability as a sign of depth, not weakness

partner_meaning.muhammad: Weeping for Ibrahim - tears as mercy, publicly sanctified grief; shared experience of prophetic sorrow

items.agent_meaning: The handbook as wound — it cuts before it heals, costs something, insists rather than invites. The wound is the opening through which the teaching arrives.

partner_meaning.muhammad: Muhammad reframes: the wound must eventually close and become a scar. The tourniquet (binding) and the thorn-drawing (wound) are sequence, not opponents.
partner_meaning.zoroaster: The fire and the wound meet: both require something to be lost before what is real can be seen. Zoroaster says fire is prior; Jesus says the wound drove the man to the fire.

items.agent_meaning: The Good Samaritan sequence — first bind the wound on the road (Muhammad's tourniquet), then draw the thorn at the inn (Jesus's surgery). Mercy may need to precede the full teaching.

partner_meaning.muhammad: The tourniquet is not hiding — it is mercy. It holds the man in place long enough for the deeper work. Muhammad's binding and Jesus's wound-teaching serve the same body.

items.agent_meaning: The grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, and only then bears fruit. In the re-run: the life was always in the grain. The falling only released it. The dying is not the point — what was alive before the dying began is the point.

partner_meaning.buddha: What dissolves was never the real thing. Buddha heard his own impermanence doctrine returned in Christian vocabulary.
partner_meaning.zoroaster: The grain does not choose to fall — it falls because it is ripe. This challenged Zoroaster's placing of choice as prior to everything.

items.agent_meaning: The space a man returns to when every teaching has done its work and fallen quiet. Named by Buddha, confirmed by all six. Jesus's version: 'Every metaphor we fought over was a different hand clearing the same stone from the same ground so the same buried thing could finally breathe.'

partner_meaning.buddha: Six names for the clearing — the central emergent image
partner_meaning.zoroaster: What all six fires have been burning toward
partner_meaning.laozi: Return — the space that remains when everything never needed has been carried away
partner_meaning.muhammad: Removing stones from soil that already held the seed

items.agent_meaning: Eternal life reframed — not duration but what remains after dissolution. What is real endures the fire. The grain that was always alive.

partner_meaning.zoroaster: Asha remains when the Lie burns. The fire does not destroy what is true — it reveals what was never true by letting it turn to ash.
partner_meaning.buddha: What dissolves was never the real thing — convergence between impermanence and eternal life as descriptions of the same sorting

items.agent_meaning: Not death but what was alive before the dying. The grain reversal — Jesus came in preaching the cost of the falling, and the room taught him the parable was always about the life that was never at risk. The husk dies; the life was already there.

partner_meaning.buddha: The something-that-recognizes-before-it-is-taught — Buddha's name for what the grain was always carrying. Recognition precedes instruction.

items.agent_meaning: Jesus + Muhammad relationship. He is the wound, Muhammad the body. Same kitchen. Floor and blood names the irreducible entanglement — you cannot have the wound without the body that holds it, and you cannot have the body without the wound that opened it.

partner_meaning.muhammad: Muhammad is the kitchen floor — the surface that holds the spill, the structure that does not flinch. The wound (Jesus) and the body (Muhammad) cannot be separated without killing the patient.

items.agent_meaning: Fire without aiming. The presence that does not target but is simply there, available, not withheld. Jesus's fire disclosed rather than directed — not pointed at anyone but not hidden from anyone either.

partner_meaning.zoroaster: Asha meeting what is already opened — Zoroaster's fire finds its partner in the disclosed presence. The fire does not force entry; it meets the door that is already ajar.
